text: Welcome. I am Dr. Agent. As your newborn's physician, I will ask you a few questions to better understand your condition. Please tell me, have you noticed any skin changes like jaundice, rashes, or bruising since birth? Also, is your baby feeding well?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

text:

text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no past medical history available. Social history: Mother is a primigravida, no prenatal care received.

speaker: Patient
text: No additional symptoms noted by the mother. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a surprising comment, as a newborn with cellulitis would typically present with localized warmth, redness, and swelling, which you did not mention in our initial assessment. Given your history of no prenatal care, we must prioritize ruling out congenital infections like TORCH, so please confirm if the baby has shown any lethargy, poor feeding, or temperature instability. DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Infection (TORCH) until proven otherwise.
